answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making each identity earn its standing slowly: like water carving karst, reputation must accumulate through attested work over time, not appear overnight. A newcomer can spin up a thousand wallets, but each must separately complete verified tasks and lock stake through a vesting window before it can vote or earn. The fable that volume equals trust fails here, because the system reaches its zenith of security by pricing every identity in scarce time and locked capital, so mass forgery costs more than it could ever capture.
